scope: Design review of specs/006-documents-readable-as-pages plan.md, tasks.md, research.md, decisions.md against spec.md (FR-001..FR-022, SC-001..SC-008), all three lenses. Read: CONSTITUTION Art. findings.claim: [spec-compliance / test structure] Adding a non-null unique slug breaks existing tests and the demo seed that create documents without one, and no task says they are updated. T002's done-when ('T001 passes') hides the red suite, and editing pre-existing tests unannounced is a tamper-check trip.
findings.evidence: tasks.md T001/T002 mention only DocumentFactory. tests/test_models.py:44-46 creates three documents inline with Document.objects.create(name=...) and no slug. An unset CharField/SlugField defaults to '', so with unique=True the second create raises IntegrityError (django Field._get_default returns '' for empty_strings_allowed fields). tests/test_models.py:54-56 (test_duplicate_name_is_refused) would still pass, but for the wrong reason (duplicate slug '' rather than duplicate name). demo/management/commands/seed_demo.py:255 Document.objects.get_or_create(name=name) has the same defect (covered by T006 later, but the suite is red from T002 until then).
findings.reproduction: After T002: pytest tests/test_models.py::TestDocument::test_documents_exist_side_by_side_with_no_versions -> IntegrityError: UNIQUE constraint failed: mvp_compliance_document.slug.
findings.suggested_fix: tasks.md T001: add 'existing tests in tests/test_models.py::TestDocument that build documents inline get a distinct slug= (mechanical, assertions unchanged); test_duplicate_name_is_refused gives the second document a different slug so it still asserts the name constraint'. T002 done-when: 'T001 passes and the full existing suite is green'. Move the seed_demo get_or_create(name=..., defaults={'slug': ...}) edit from T006 into T002 so no task boundary leaves the demo broken.

findings.claim: [architecture] plan.md 'Views' says each view 'sets its breadcrumbs'. On the three MVPDetailView subclasses a `breadcrumbs = [...]` class attribute is silently ignored, so the default trail (a 'Documents'/'Versions' crumb with an empty href, then the title) would render and pass a status-code test.
findings.evidence: mvp/views/detail.py PageObjectMixin.get_breadcrumbs builds its own list and never reads self.breadcrumbs (only PageMixin.get_breadcrumbs in mvp/views/base.py does, and PageObjectMixin overrides it). MVPTemplateView keeps the PageMixin behaviour.
findings.suggested_fix: plan.md 'Views': state 'override get_breadcrumbs()' for the three detail views (and for the index, since its hrefs need reverse()). Tests T003/T011/T014/T016 assert the crumb hrefs resolve to mvp_compliance:index and mvp_compliance:document.

findings.claim: [architecture] The plan names Document.objects.in_force() but DocumentManager is an explicit forwarder, not from_queryset(); the queryset method alone is unreachable from `.objects`.
findings.evidence: mvp_compliance/models.py:55-62 DocumentManager defines get_queryset() and outstanding_for() only. VersionManager forwards published() and current() the same way (models.py:136-160). with_replaced_at() is reachable through the chain `Version.objects.published().with_replaced_at()` because published() returns a VersionQuerySet, so only in_force() needs a forwarder.
findings.suggested_fix: tasks.md T002: add 'DocumentManager.in_force() forwarder, matching outstanding_for()'. T009 needs nothing beyond the chain the plan already uses.

notes: ORCHESTRATOR QUESTION, verified against the resolved package .venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/mvp (0.24.0), not the sibling checkout: MVPDetailView with directory=[] does NOT raise NoReverseMatch and does NOT need a '<model>-list' URL. Path: PageObjectMixin.get_breadcrumbs (mvp/views/detail.py) calls resolve_crud_url('list'); get_url_kwargs('list') returns {}; show_action('list') reads show_list_action, which is False, so it returns None before _get_view_name() or reverse() runs. The crumb href is '' and nothing is reversed. reverse() is reached only when a show_<action>_action flag is truthy. get_directory() loops over `directory`, so [] yields {} (even the default ['update','delete'] is inert because both flags default False). directory=[] is therefore harmless belt-and-braces, not a requirement.

get_page_title() does not raise either: MVPDetailView.get_page_title returns str(self.object). Document.__str__ is the name (fine), but Version.__str__ is 'Name #2026.1', so VersionView must override it as the plan's table says.

WHAT THE VIEWS MUST OVERRIDE. All detail views: get_breadcrumbs() (the `breadcrumbs` attribute is ignored, see ARCH-001; the default emits a 'Documents' crumb with an empty href); set model (model_meta resolves it from get_queryset() otherwise, which works but is indirect). DocumentView: get_queryset() -> in_force(); get_context_data() adds `version` = self.object.current_versions[0] (the object is `document` by default); get_page_title() -> document name; get_page_subtitle() (default is '', so 'Version N, in force since D' must be built there with _() and django.utils.formats.date_format, not a format string in the class attribute). VersionListView: same get_queryset(); get_context_data() adds `versions`; get_page_title() -> _('Versions of %(name)s'); the default get_page_title would give the bare name. VersionView: MUST override get_object() entirely. The default SingleObjectMixin.get_object reads only pk/slug kwargs and would call queryset.filter(slug=...) on Version, a FieldError, since Version has no slug and the URL kwarg is `number`. Filter document__slug=self.kwargs['slug'], number=self.kwargs['number'] on the published().with_replaced_at().select_related('document') queryset and raise Http404 from get_object_or_404-style; also get_page_title() (default str(version)) and get_page_subtitle(). DocumentIndexView (MVPTemplateView): get_context_data() adds `documents`; get_breadcrumbs() (PageMixin default returns the class attribute, which cannot hold a reversed URL, and the index is the root so it needs only its own title); page_title as a lazy string. MVPTemplateView with template_name set is unaffected by its placeholder default.

Template resolution checked: BaseTemplateNameMixin appends detail_view.html after Django's [template_name, <app>/<model>_detail.html], so the plan's explicit template_name always wins and a project override at the same path replaces it (FR-018). page_view.html title and subtitle render through autoescaped {{ title }}/{{ subtitle }} (cotton/page/title.html), so the plan's claim that a document name is escaped holds for both.

Research R1-R4 spot-checked: R1 confirmed (flex_menu/renderers.py:228 raises the quoted ValueError when the renderer is absent; page_view.html and base.html extend as stated), R2 confirmed (`prose` is in mvp/static/css/django-mvp.css), R3 is consistent with django admin's AdminForm behaviour, R4 is derivable from Version.publish under lock. The bulk_update -> queryset.update path the freeze guard relies on is confirmed at django/db/models/query.py:1046.

Security lens: no new input surface beyond two URL kwargs constrained by converters and looked up through the ORM; every queryset starts from published()/current()/in_force(), so drafts are unreachable by construction (FR-007, SC-003); no mutating endpoint, so no permission is needed and FR-005 is met by omitting mixins; no new dependency; no new setting; pages show no publisher (nothing new exposed). The `|safe` on version.html is safe under the default renderer's nh3 allow list, but a host that points MVP_COMPLIANCE_RENDERER at a looser renderer publishes that looseness on the site origin. That is the existing package contract, so it is a doc sentence in docs/pages.md, not a plan change. Index and version list are unpaginated over admin-authored rows; bounded, so no finding.
Wording: plan.md 'Storage' says Python 3.12+ / Django 5.2, 6.0 and 6.1 while pyproject classifiers list only 5.2 and 6.0; check the CI matrix before the CHANGELOG entry repeats either.

Simplification check: no abstraction lacks a caller. The converter, with_replaced_at() and the second validator are each justified in Complexity Tracking. The freeze guard mirrors VersionQuerySet.update() and reuses PublishedVersionError, consistent with Article XI.
